evidence: The A page declares qm-math-oscillator as the first entry of its requires list. Every in-run mathematical supplier of the page resolves either to a batch-36 item recorded ready on that page (the two diagonal-operator items) or to the batch-35 item thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators reached through batch 36; see the item rows below for the exact clauses used. The engine's batch-dependency-levels digest lists batch 38 with requires ["36"], and batch 36 itself requires batch 35, so both supplier batches are complete before this batch by construction.

The B page declares requires [qm-math-intervals-and-contacts]; all three examples depend on parent-page items (the twisted-periodic momentum operator, the sine completeness theorem, the delta interface operator and its unique bound state) as recorded in their deps arrays.

Used at [F3] and steps 3.1-4.1: the diagonal operator of the batch-36 lemma is self-adjoint with domain {x : sum_n lambda_n^2 |<x,e_n>|^2 < infinity} and the finite spans form a graph core; the domain computation and the identification of A with the diagonal operator in step 3.1 use exactly the statement of that lemma, whose hypotheses (a complete orthonormal family and real numbers lambda_n) are met by the eigenfamily of step 1.1.

Used at [F3] and step 4.1: the spectrum of the diagonal operator is the closure of the sequence (nu_n); applied to the entries mu_n = c + nu_n^{-1} this gives the closure statement of step 4.1, and the supplier's statement that the closure is attained when the entries tend to infinity is the reason the eigenvalue set is closed there.

Used at [F2] and steps 1.1, 3.1, 6.1-7.1: the diagonal operator A_D associated with the sine family (e_n) and the numbers lambda_n = (n pi/L)^2 is self-adjoint with domain {x : sum_n lambda_n^2|<x,e_n>|^2 < infinity}, A_De_n = lambda_n e_n, and the finite spans are a graph core; the theorem identifies that operator with the Dirichlet Laplacian.

Used at [F2] and step 6.1: sigma(A_D) is the closure of {lambda_n : n >= 1}; since lambda_n = (n pi/L)^2 is injective and tends to infinity, the closure is the set itself and the eigenvalues are simple, which is the spectrum statement of clause (b).

Used at [F5] and steps 3.1: the restriction S of P_theta to the span of the characters is the finite-support diagonal operator with respect to the complete orthonormal family (phi_n) and the real numbers kappa_n, so the supplier's uniqueness statement gives P_theta = T and the displayed coefficient domain.

Used at [F5] and step 3.1: sigma(P_theta) is the closure of {kappa_n}; because kappa_n -> +/- infinity there is no finite accumulation point, so the spectrum is exactly the eigenvalue set {kappa_n : n in Z}.

Used at [F2] and step 2.1: the diagonal operator Delta_D associated with the complete orthonormal product family (e_nm) and the real numbers mu_nm is self-adjoint with Delta_De_nm = mu_nm e_nm, and uniqueness of coefficients identifies ker(Delta_D - mu) as the span of the basis vectors with mu_nm = mu.

Used at [F1] and steps 2.2, 3.1-3.2: clause (b) with d=1, c=4 pi^2, b=0 gives the free operator A_0 on D(A_0) = H^2(R) with A_0u = -D^2u (and self-adjointness), which is the operator whose resolvent kernel G_z the lemma computes.

Used at [F3] and step 2.1: clause (b) supplies the free operator A_0 with two-sided resolvent R_0(z), and the interface correction u = r + cG_z is built from it; the relation (A_0 - z)r = f and the decay of G_z used there are the content of that clause together with the free-line lemma.

Used at [F1] and step 1.1: clause (c) with d=1 and the free operator of clause (b), for the bounded measurable real potential V with |V| <= U and support [-a,a], gives that H = H_0 + M_V is self-adjoint on D(H_0) = H^2(R) with real spectrum, which is clause (a).
